symptom: `join finish; merge finish;` (a merge only one path enters) was written by exec and then described as nothing, with '-- WARNING: the merge at (1330, 350) is not represented in this description ... re-executing this MDL DELETES it' (mendixlabs/mxcli#923 MF_RT_Chain). The warning had also stopped being true: `create or modify` from the description reports Unchanged and keeps the merge.
cause: traverseFlow walks through any unlabelled merge that no split pairs with, so a one-input merge left no trace in the text; droppedMergeWarnings then flagged it with wording from before modify-in-place compared descriptions instead of rebuilding
insight: Only the MAIN LINE (indent 0) can spell it back: there a `merge` after a `join` has no open path, so the builder draws exactly one edge into it. In a branch body the branch loop would add its own fall-through edge (no pathOpen guard), and MDL-FLOW04 bans labels in loop bodies, so those keep the (reworded) warning. Labels are minted lazily in walk order (junction1, …) so unused candidates leave no gaps. Two traps: assertDescriptionRebuildsGraph decided 'is this a whole statement?' with strings.Contains(src, "create "), which a warning mentioning `create or modify` defeats (fixed to a line check); and the graph comparison is merge-blind, so a merge-count assertion is needed to see the fix at all. Verified on PedApp 11.13.0: main binary 1 warning, fixed 0; describe -> exec Unchanged as modify AND as replace; 3 merges before and after.
